verdict.rationale: Glama documents a directory API for its MCP registry. An OpenAPI 3.0.3 spec titled "Glama MCP API" covers /v1 paths for servers and connectors. It is machine-discoverable from llms.txt and from an RFC 9727 /.well-known/api-catalog, and a hosted reference (e.g. list-mcp-servers) provides code samples and a Try-it panel. The OpenAPI probe's 404s at common guessed paths do not contradict this, because the spec lives at /api/mcp/openapi.json. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that agents successfully query the API, and explicit evidence that tool-level listings are exposed via the API beyond the reference page's claim of capability inspection.

support.subject: As an AI agent, I can query the platform's registry or catalog through a documented API to discover servers and tools programmatically

citations.quote: Glama publishes an OpenAPI 3.0.3 document for its MCP directory API (info title "Glama MCP API", /v1 paths for servers, connectors, instances, usage)

The RFC 9727 API catalog (application/linkset+json) links the machine spec (service-desc) and the hosted reference (service-doc), completing a fully machine-discoverable chain from the well-known path.
